title: Heirlooms & Blooms Pairs Vintage Finds With Cut Flowers On 50th Street - kkam.com
content: There are certain businesses in Lubbock where the name pretty much tells you what you're getting. I recently came across this place and immediately wondered the same thing you probably are: Are we talking antiques or flowers? Heirlooms & Blooms is a locally operated shop located at 4620 50th Street in Lubbock, and it's listed as both an antique store and florist. That's a combination I don't run across very often. The "heirlooms" side gives shoppers the chance to browse antiques and vintage merchandise, while the "blooms" portion of the business brings flowers and floral products into the mix. And frankly, the two actually make a lot of sense together. If you're looking for something unique for the house, or maybe a gift that doesn't involve wandering around a giant chain store for 45 minutes, this seems like the kind of place worth exploring. One interesting thing about Heirlooms & Blooms is that it doesn't appear to be trying to become the Amazon of Lubbock antique stores. Its website is pretty simple, featuring Home, Catalog and Contact sections. As of this writing, the online catalog doesn't have products listed for purchase. In other words, this looks like one of those places you're actually supposed to walk into and look around. With antiques especially, that's half the fun. You never really know what's going to be sitting around the next corner. Heirlooms & Blooms is located right on 50th Street, so we're not talking about some shop hidden 30 miles outside of town. It's right here in Lubbock on one of our busiest streets. Current hours listed by the business are Monday through Saturday from 9:30 a.m. until 5:30 p.m., with the store closed on Sundays. In an era when we can see virtually everything a store sells before we ever leave the couch, Heirlooms & Blooms feels like the kind of old-fashioned Lubbock business where you might actually have to walk through the door to find out what they've got. And when antiques are involved, that's exactly how it should be.

Three US-listed names capture the economics of that supply chain, and their most recent quarters make the setup concrete. NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA | NVDA Price Prediction) designs the accelerators that train and run the largest AI models. In plain language, NVIDIA sells the compute engine, plus the switching fabric that connects thousands of those engines into an AI factory. The company outsources manufacturing, handing designs to Taiwan Semiconductor. The August 26 report was the tell. Q2 FY27 revenue reached $96.22 billion, up 105.85% year over year, with data center revenue of $89.02 billion growing 117%. Non-GAAP EPS of $2.22 beat the $2.0887 consensus by 6.29%, and Q3 revenue guidance came in at $108.0 billion plus or minus 2%, excluding any data center compute revenue from China. Content per gigawatt is expanding as fast as the number of gigawatts being built. NVIDIA cited roughly $18 billion per gigawatt on Hopper, $25 billion on Blackwell, and $40 billion on Vera Rubin. A slower Vera Rubin ramp or a memory hiccup would leave a lot of committed capital exposed. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM) is the world’s dominant pure-play foundry. TSMC manufactures the designs that NVIDIA, Broadcom, AMD, and Apple hand over. When observers say “leading-edge silicon,” they largely mean wafers coming out of TSMC’s 3nm and 2nm nodes. Every AI chip designer in this article depends on it. Q2 was a demonstration of pricing power. Revenue reached $40.20 billion with a 67.7% gross margin, diluted EPS of $4.31 beat the $3.8866 consensus by 10.89%, and technologies at 7nm and below accounted for 77% of wafer revenue, with 3nm at 30% and 2nm at 3% in its first commercial quarter. title: Severe T-Strom Prompts Over 9000 Power Outages in Rochester, Leaves Downed Tree Limbs in its Wake - KDHL Radio
content: Rochester, MN (RochesterNow)- Rochester is waking up to the fallout from a severe thunderstorm Wednesday morning. See Also: Rochester Murder Suspect Back in Custody on Drug Charges The storm left thousands of power outages in its wake and caused large tree limbs to come crashing down to the ground. The city’s outdoor warning sirens sounded three times around 1:30 Wednesday morning. Storm reports are still being gathered but a 68 mph wind gust was reported around 1:30 Wednesday. The National Weather Service recorded the gust at the St. Mary’s Heliport. A 61 mph wind gust was recorded around 1:30 a.m. at the Rochester Airport and another 61 mph gust occurred near the Highland Ridge neighborhood which is east of 50th Ave. SE and north of Hwy. 52 southeast of Rochester. There was also a report of a water intrusion into the Mayo Clinic expansion construction zone in downtown Rochester, according to the National Weather Service. Rochester Public Utilities (RPU) says 62 outages are impacting 7970 customers as of 7:20 Wednesday morning. RPU reported as many as 9400 power outages around 6:00 Wednesday morning. “Our crews are working to restore power as quickly and safely as possible. For your safety, please stay clear of any downed power lines and always assume they are energized. Thank you for your patience as our crews work to restore service. We will continue to share updates here as more information becomes available,” an RPU Facebook post says.

title: RGB International expects stronger 2H on improved machine sales, TSM recovery - KLSE Screener
content: Have a question, feedback, or need assistance with your account? KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 1): RGB International Bhd (KL:RGB) expects its earnings to improve in the second half of 2026, underpinned by stronger sales of gaming machines and improved performance from its technical support and management (TSM) business. The optimism is supported by the delivery of the remaining 1,700 gaming machines under its 3,000-machine target for the year and a recovery in TSM business, according to its chief operating officer for leisure, Chuah Eng Meng. Eng Meng said the group is expected to grow its sales, services and marketing (SSM) business with additional integrated resorts in the Philippines and is also positioned to benefit from the replacement cycle from Macau's new electronic gaming machine technical standards. “We submitted our tender last month for one of the major casinos in Macau. The tender is expected to conclude by the third quarter and deliver by the fourth quarter,” he added. The replacement programme is expected to roll out progressively over the next one to two years as the casino operator upgrades its gaming floors. On TSM, Eng Meng said the business will be “bottomed out” as RGB optimises operations by shifting machines towards better-performing outlets and exiting loss-making outlets. “For the ones that are non-profitable in the Philippines, we are negotiating with other sites that are performing really well to add on more machines there, moving from non-performing outlets to better-performing ones,” he said. He added that relocating machines requires regulatory approval, which RGB had obtained. RGB’s weaker quarterly earnings were mainly due to lower margins in its SSM division, following discounts given for bulk orders from customers in the Philippines. RGB recorded a 26.3% year-on-year decline in net profit to RM10.33 million in the second quarter ended June 30, 2026 (2QFY2026), despite revenue rising 15% to RM109.63 million, from RM94.95 million a year ago. This brings its net profit for the first half of FY2026 to RM19.4 million, down by 26.5% from RM26.41 million, while revenue increased 16.9% to RM197.01 million. Its executive director, Chuah Hui Jing, said discounts and additional payment terms were offered to support customers placing large orders. “It's only for this year because they are buying a big order. Going forward, this is not the norm, it's just a one-off thing,” Hui Jing added. RGB is also expanding into the digital gaming business in the Philippines, which expects to begin contributing to group earnings within one to two years. “We expect this segment to start contributing to group earnings in the next one, two years,” said Hui Jing, adding that time would be needed to build marketing traction and attract players to the platform. RGB's digital gaming business comprises three offerings – game content, game aggregation and white-label or managed services. The group said the white-label and turnkey model could provide the larger revenue opportunity, as it operates on a revenue-sharing basis, while requiring relatively little capital expenditure. The white-label and managed-services offering is aimed at integrated-resort (IR) operators that want to launch an online gaming brand but lack the in-house technology, operational expertise or team to do so. Under this model, RGB and its operating partner would provide and manage the online platform for the operator, with RGB earning a share of the revenue. “The bulk of revenue is if we're able to get the turnkey white-label solution, because that portion is a 20-30% revenue share. "In the online space, GGR (gross gaming revenue) can be a lot higher. We have already put our bid for one of the IRs and are in very extensive talks, plus two more in initial discussions,” Hui Jing shared. “There's no big CapEx [for this new digital gaming ventures]. Marketing expenses are covered by our operating partner who has a very big marketing arm in the Philippines. title: TSM stock gets a fresh target hike as revenue and capex expectations rise - AD HOC NEWS
content: TSM stock is back in focus on August 31, 2026, after a new analyst target hike highlights stronger revenue growth and higher capital spending plans at Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company. TSM stock (US8740391003) is drawing renewed attention as of August 31, 2026, after a fresh analyst note lifted the target price on Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company and emphasized stronger revenue growth and higher capital spending plans for the chipmaker. The latest call points to an expected increase in TSMC's 2026 revenue outlook to 40% year-on-year growth in U.S. dollar terms, alongside a planned rise in capital expenditure to $56 billion, at the top of a previously guided $52 billion to $56 billion range. This combination of faster growth and heavier investment sets the tone for how investors are reassessing the long-term trajectory of TSM stock. A key catalyst on August 31, 2026, is a report stating that analysts have raised their target stock price for TSMC by 12% to NT$2,888, citing improved revenue prospects and better pricing power across its core chip manufacturing business. This target move is framed around expectations that the company will formally lift its guidance at an upcoming earnings conference call. In that call, which is anticipated for the next reporting cycle, TSMC is expected to raise its 2026 revenue expectations to 40% year-on-year growth, compared with an earlier guide that had been above 30% in U.S. dollar terms. The shift from a “above 30%” range to a clear 40% growth figure is a quantified upgrade that underscores how demand for advanced nodes and artificial intelligence-related chips is feeding through to the top line. On the investment side, the same report highlights that TSMC plans to increase its capital expenditure for 2026 to $56 billion. This represents the high end of a previously signaled band of $52 billion to $56 billion, indicating that management is willing to commit more cash to expand and upgrade capacity in response to robust customer orders and long-term contracts in areas such as high-performance computing and data centers. The 12% uplift in the NT$2,888 target level gives investors a concrete benchmark for how the new expectations are being translated into valuation. A target change of that magnitude, tied directly to a 40% revenue growth assumption and a full-weight $56 billion capex plan, provides a visible comparison against earlier, more conservative assumptions on both growth and investment intensity. The stronger guidance for future revenue and capital expenditure sits on top of very robust recent financial performance. In the latest quarter covering the April-to-June 2026 period, TSMC’s financial data show net profit of NT$706.56 billion, up 77.4% from a year earlier and 23.4% from the prior quarter. This year-over-year gain of 77.4% and sequential increase of 23.4% give investors a clear numerical sense of how sharply profitability has accelerated. Earnings per share in the same second quarter of 2026 climbed to NT$27.25, compared with NT$15.36 a year earlier and NT$22.08 in the first quarter of 2026. The progression from NT$15.36 to NT$27.25 represents an EPS increase of NT$11.89, while the move from NT$22.08 in the first quarter to NT$27.25 in the second quarter marks a sequential gain of NT$5.17 per share. These comparisons show both strong year-on-year growth and meaningful quarter-on-quarter momentum. Over the first half of 2026, TSMC posted net profit of NT$1.28 trillion, an increase of 68.3% from a year earlier. In the same six-month period, EPS rose to NT$49.32 from NT$29.30 a year before, an improvement of NT$20.02 per share. The combination of NT$1.28 trillion in profit and a 68.3% gain year-on-year reinforces the idea that the company’s earnings base is expanding quickly even before the higher 2026 revenue and capex guidance fully play out. The earnings strength is also visible in how TSMC rewards its workforce. For the second quarter of 2026, employee bonuses totaled NT$36 billion, more than 50% higher than in the same quarter a year earlier. Across the first half of 2026, bonuses reached NT$70.35 billion, up 54.3% year-on-year. These figures reflect both the company’s record earnings and its policy of sharing gains with employees, which can help support retention and motivation in a highly competitive semiconductor talent market. While the detailed revenue breakdown for the quarter is not fully spelled out in every summary, separate reporting on TSMC’s most recent quarterly release points to a 40% jump in revenue to $40.2 billion and a 77% jump in profit to $22.3 billion. These numbers align closely with the NT$ figures cited in local financial data and give an additional U.S. dollar context for international investors who follow TSM stock via the ADR. The 40% revenue increase to $40.2 billion and the 77% profit increase to $22.3 billion provide a direct parallel to the 77.4% net profit growth and 68.3% first-half profit gain reported in Taiwan dollars. This dual-currency perspective helps investors who model the stock in U.S. dollars reconcile the magnitude of the earnings acceleration with the company’s guidance for U.S.-dollar revenue growth. Importantly, the same coverage notes that the strong quarterly results were followed by a notable share-price reaction on TSMC’s home market. On the day after the release, TSMC shares dropped 7.3%, leading to the largest single-day point decline on record for Taiwan’s benchmark TAIEX index. For ADR investors, this episode illustrates how even outstanding earnings can be followed by profit-taking or shifts in sentiment, particularly when valuations are high and expectations have been rising for several quarters. This kind of move also shows why the new 12% target hike to NT$2,888 matters: it gives a refreshed valuation anchor after a period in which the home-market price showed that strong fundamentals do not always guarantee a smooth upward path for the share price. The gap between a 7.3% post-earnings drop and a higher target level underscores the tension between short-term trading reactions and medium-term valuation views. The higher capital expenditure guidance for 2026 is closely tied to expectations around artificial intelligence infrastructure and advanced chip demand. The report highlighting TSMC’s plan to spend $56 billion points out that the increase to the top of the previously expected $52 billion to $56 billion range reflects strong AI capital spending and robust chip demand from clients building data centers and high-performance computing systems. In earlier communications, TSMC had indicated a lower capex range of $52 billion to $56 billion, alongside a full-year revenue growth forecast “above 30%” in U.S. dollar terms. By lifting revenue growth expectations to 40% and capex to the $56 billion high point, the company is effectively signaling that demand for its most advanced process nodes is stronger than initially anticipated and that it intends to invest aggressively to stay ahead in capacity and technology. The same reporting emphasizes that TSMC’s competitive position in foundry services remains strong because of its production capacity, its access to advanced EUV lithography equipment, and its lead in cutting-edge process nodes. As a result, competitive pressure from rivals such as Samsung and Intel in contract manufacturing is not expected to significantly erode TSMC’s position in the near term, even as those competitors scale up their own foundry offerings. For investors looking at TSM stock, the combination of 40% expected revenue growth, a $56 billion capex plan, and reaffirmed competitive advantages in EUV technology and leading-edge nodes form the core of the long-term investment narrative. The numbers show not only that current profits are strong but also that the company is committing substantial resources to ensure that this strength can be sustained and potentially extended in coming years. Behind the headline numbers for profit and capex, TSMC’s business is increasingly driven by the chips it manufactures for artificial intelligence workloads and cloud data centers. These products, fabricated on cutting-edge process technologies such as 3-nanometer nodes, are typically designed by major fabless chip designers and then produced by TSMC in high volumes. The advanced AI and data-center chips emphasize high transistor density, energy efficiency, and performance per watt, characteristics that are critical for large-scale training and inference workloads in modern AI models. As demand for these capabilities grows among cloud providers, social platforms, and enterprise software vendors, TSMC’s role as a manufacturing partner for these designs becomes more central to the broader technology ecosystem. For TSM stock, this means that the company’s revenue and profit trajectory is increasingly linked to long-term trends in AI adoption, data-center expansion, and high-performance computing applications. The 40% revenue growth expectation for 2026, paired with a $56 billion capex plan, reflects not just cyclical chip demand but structural growth in these segments, which require ongoing investments in capacity and process innovation. As of late August 2026, TSM stock continues to trade with a valuation that incorporates both the strong recent earnings and the upgraded guidance for revenue and capex. Market data pages for comparable semiconductor and technology names show share-price levels framed by daily percentage moves, trading volumes, and 52-week ranges, giving investors a way to contextualize TSM’s latest moves against broader sector dynamics. In the recent trading sessions following the quarter and guidance updates, TSMC’s home-market shares have experienced both strong rallies and sharp pullbacks, including the 7.3% drop that weighed on the TAIEX index. For ADR holders, the key takeaway is that volatility can be elevated around major earnings and guidance events, even when the underlying fundamentals are improving quickly. Against this backdrop, the new 12% target hike to NT$2,888, anchored in a 40% revenue growth expectation and a $56 billion capex commitment, provides a clear numerical reference for how some analysts view the medium-term potential of TSMC. Whether the share price converges toward that level will depend on future quarters delivering on the promised growth and on how global markets digest both AI-related enthusiasm and macroeconomic risks. For now, TSM stock represents a semiconductor name backed by record profits, rapidly rising earnings per share, and aggressive investment in capacity, all set against a backdrop of strong AI and data-center demand. The latest quarter’s NT$706.56 billion net profit and NT$27.25 EPS, combined with the 68.3% first-half profit increase to NT$1.28 trillion and the reshaped 2026 guidance, give investors a detailed numerical picture of why the stock remains central to discussions about the global chip cycle. title: McDonald's in Northern Colorado May Have Closed For Good - Fort Collins Country Radio
content: It is always sad to see a restaurant close in Northern Colorado. Customers are upset that they can't have some of their favorite food anymore, or they have to find a new location to visit if it is a chain. Many places have been closing recently, and they typically do so due to underperformance, perhaps for upgrades, or because a chain has decided to close select locations. Sometimes places are forced to close for reasons that are unexpected, and this recently happened to a fast food location in the area. A fast food chain location in Northern Colorado may have closed for good without anyone realizing it, as signs point towards it not reopening ever. If you search the McDonald's located at 1273 Grand Market Ave in Berthoud, Google will tell you that it is currently open, depending on what time of day you search it, but anyone who has driven by knows this is not the case. For months, the store has been closed, claiming the location is closed for maintenance. The store was set to reopen earlier this summer, but that never happened. Since then, many have been asking when the location will open, but recently some things changed that point towards the store never opening again. As seen in the pictures above, the 'M' logo that represents McDonald's has been removed from the building, but that isn't the only sign pointing towards permanent closure. While signs being removed is not a good sign, the menus for the drive-thru have also been taken down, and if you look in the pictures above, you will notice all the equipment in the kitchen has been removed as well. The windows for the drive-thru have been boarded up, and it looks like the building will not be used anytime soon. This should not be too surprising, though, as Taco Bell in the same parking lot recently was forced to close by the city of Berthoud due to the foundation not being safe. While Taco Bell states they are temporarily closed, McDonald's seems to have decided to go a different route.

title: Driver Who Crashed Into Two Businesses In North Adams Identified And Charged - WUPE
content: The driver of a black Silverado pickup truck faces charges of negligent operation of a motor vehicle and a marked-lanes violation after crashing into a storefront in North Adams, which closed two businesses indefinitely. The Berkshire Eagle reports John Miner, a man in his 40s, made a turn from St. Anthony’s Drive onto Marshall Street. As he accelerated, the truck's rear end began to fishtail as it lost traction. According to Chief Mark Bailey, witnesses at the scene reported hearing a vehicle accelerate excessively before the crash. Miner was not wearing a seatbelt, so he had to be transported to the hospital, while his passenger, who was wearing her seatbelt, was treated at the scene. The condition of Miner's injuries is still uncertain. The crash happened at around 10 p.m., when both businesses were closed for the evening. However, they have since been boarded up and will remain closed until further notice. Affected businesses include Brewsters, a thrift store that opened in December, where the truck crashed into the front window, and Tres Ninos Taqueria, where the side window was damaged on impact. Building Inspector William Meranti stated that the majority of the damage affected the glass, with only minor harm observed in the structural beams. "We're very lucky that the vehicle missed the structural columns - building owner David Carver  of Scarafoni Associates Carver said it's too early to estimate the expenses or schedule for reconstruction. However, he noted that the glass storefronts and the historic front door will require custom fabrication. He is developing a repair plan, and the next step is coordinating with the insurance company. He concluded by praising the city of North Adams for their quick response.
